5.6: Seven androgynous entities became manifest in Chaos. They possess their masculine names as well as their feminine names:
5.7: The feminine name is Pronoia, Sambathas, which means “week,” and his son is named Yao, his feminine name being Rulership. Sabaoth, his feminine name is Divinity. Adonaios, his feminine name is Kingship. Elaios, his feminine name is Jealousy. Oraios, his feminine name is Wealth, and Astaphaios, his [feminine] name

6.1: [ 102 ] is Sophia.
6.2: These are the seven forces pertaining to the seven heavens of Chaos, and they were born as androgynous entities, congruent with the deathless structure that existed before them, in accord with the desire of Pistis, namely, that the likeness of what had existed from the beginning would rule until the end.
6.3: You will discover the power these names exert, as well as the force of the male entities, in the (book) The Archangelic (Nature) of the Prophet Moses , and that of the names of the female entities in the First Book of Noraia .
6.4: Now, the Primal Parent Yaldabaoth, given that he possessed great authorities, created heavens for each one of his offspring by means of verbal articulation, creating them good, as dwelling-places, and in each of the heavens he created great glories, seven times as excellent. Thrones, and palaces, and temples, as well as chariots and virginal spirits (all the way) up to an unseen one, and their glories, each one possessing these in its (respective) heaven: mighty hosts of gods, and lords, and angels, and archangels, myriads without number, in order that they would serve.
6.5: The narration of these events you will find in an exact description in the First Narration of Oraia .
6.6: And they were finished, as far as from this heaven up to the sixth heaven, which is that of Sophia.
6.7:
This heaven and earth were assailed by the mischief-maker who dwelt below all of them, and the six heavens trembled fiercely, because the hosts of Chaos knew who had assailed the heaven located beneath them, and when Pistis became aware of the fracture caused by the mischief-maker, she sent out her spirit and tied him and thrust him down into Tartaros.

[From that day], the heaven, together with

7.1:
[ 103 ] its earth, has established itself by means of Sophia, the daughter of Yaldabaoth, she who dwells below all of them.

The Transgression of Yaldabaoth
7.2: When the heavens had established themselves together with their hosts and all of their government, the Primal Parent grew arrogant, and he was worshiped by the entire host of angels, and all the gods and their angels offered praise and worship to him, and he was elated, and repeatedly bragged, saying to them: “I am self-sufficient.”
7.3: He said, “I am the one who is God, and except me there is nothing else that exists,” and when he had said this, he transgressed against all the deathless ones who use verbal articulation, and they accused him over it.
7.4: When Pistis then witnessed the impiety of the chief archon, she became enraged. She who was unseen said: “You are in error, Samael,” that is, “Blind God.” “There is a deathless man of light who existed before you did, and he will become manifest among the forms you have shaped. He will tread on you in scorn, like a potter’s vessel is tread upon, and you will plummet down to your mother, the Abyss, together with those who are your own, because at the completion of all of your works, the whole deficiency that has been exposed by the truth will be abrogated, and its existence will end, and it will be as though it had never been.”
7.5:
Upon saying this, Pistis manifested the likeness of her greatness in the waters, and having done this, she retreated back up into her light.

Sabaoth Sings Praises to Pistis
7.6: When Sabaoth, the son of Yaldabaoth, had heard the voice of Pistis, he sang praises to her, and he denounced his father [and mother]

8.1: [ 104 ] at the bidding of Pistis, and he praised her on account of her having taught them concerning the deathless man and his light. Pistis Sophia next pointed her finger and poured onto him some of the light from her (own) light, as a denunciation of his father. When Sabaoth had been illuminated, he obtained great authority against all the hosts of Chaos. From that day, he has been called “Lord of Hosts.”
8.2: He despised his father, the Darkness, and his mother, the Abyss, and hated his sister, the thought of the Primal Parent, who had moved back and forth over the waters, and on account of his light, all of the authorities of Chaos grew jealous of him, and when they had become troubled, they waged a great war in the seven heavens.
8.3: When Pistis Sophia then had witnessed the war, from her light she sent out seven archangels to Sabaoth. They bore him up to the seventh heaven. They stood in front of him as attendants. She furthermore sent to him three additional archangels, and established for him the kingdom that is over everyone, in order that he could dwell over the twelve gods of Chaos.
8.4: Now, when Sabaoth had taken over the dwelling-place of rest as recompense for his repentance, Pistis gave him her daughter Zoe as well, together with great authority, in order that she could teach him concerning everything that exists in the eighth heaven, and because he possessed authority, before all else he constructed a palace for himself. It is immense, magnificent, seven times larger than all those that exist in the seven heavens, and in front of

9.1: [ 105 ] his palace he created a throne, which was immense, and which stood on a four-faced chariot called “Cherubin.”
9.2:
The Cherubin possess eight shapes on each of the four corners: lion forms, and calf forms, and human forms, and eagle forms, in order that all the forms have a sum of sixty-four forms, and there are seven archangels who stand in front of it. He is the eighth, and he possesses authority. All the forms have the sum of seventy-two. Additionally, from this chariot the seventy-two gods derived (their) shape, in order that they could rule over the seventy-two languages of the nations, and at that throne he additionally created serpent-like angels, called “Seraphin,” which glorify him always.

Sabaoth Creates Angels, Israel, and Jesus Christ
9.3: After this, he created an assembly of angels, countless thousands and myriads, which looked like the assembly in the eighth heaven, and a firstborn called “Israel,” that is, “the Man Who Sees God,” and another entity called “Jesus Christ,” who looks like the savior who dwells above in the eighth heaven, and who sits at his right (hand) on a holy throne, and at his left (hand), there the Virgin of the holy Spirit sits on a throne, even glorifying him, and the seven virgins stand in front of her, holding thirty harps, and lyres, and

10.1: [ 106 ] trumpets, glorifying him, and all of the angel hosts glorify him, and they praise him.
10.2: The place he sits is on a throne of light <in a> large cloud covering him, and no one dwelt with him inside the cloud except Sophia, <the daughter of> Pistis, who taught him concerning all the entities that exist inside the eighth heaven, in order to be able to create the likenesses of those entities, so that his reign could last until the consummation of the heavens of Chaos and their hosts.
10.3:
Now, Pistis Sophia separated him from the darkness and called him to her right, and she placed the Primal Parent at her left. From that day, right has been called “justice,” and left has been called “evil.” On account of this, all of them obtained an aeon in the assembly of justice, and evil stands over every created entity.

Yaldabaoth Begets Death
10.4: In this way, when the Primal Parent of Chaos witnessed his son Sabaoth and the glory he dwelt inside, and realized he was greatest of every authority of Chaos, he grew envious of him, and having grown furious, he begot Death from out of his (own) death, and he was appointed over the sixth heaven, <because> Sabaoth had been borne upwards from that place, and in this way the number of the six authorities of Chaos was reached.
10.5: Death, an androgynous entity, then mixed himself together with his (own) nature, and begot seven androgynous children. Here are the names of the male children:
10.6:
Jealousy, Fury, Tears, Moaning, Suffering, Weeping, Bitter Lamentation.

And here are the names of the female children:
10.7: Fury, Pain, Lust, Moaning, Curse, Bitterness, Argumentativeness.
10.8: They had sex with each other, and each begot seven children, which resulted in the sum of

11.1: [ 107 ] forty-nine androgynous demons.
11.2: You will discover their names and their impacts in the Book of Solomon.
11.3: And in front of these, Zoe, who dwelt with Sabaoth, created seven good androgynous forces. Here are the names of the males: the Non-Jealous One, the Blessed One, the Joyful One, the True One, the Non-Envying One, the Beloved One, the Faithful One. Additionally, regarding the females, here are their names: Peace, Gladness, Joyfulness, Blessedness, Truth, Love, Pistis, and from these powers originate many good and pure spirits.
11.4:
You will discover their impacts and their effects in the (Book of the) Structures of the Fate of Heaven Beneath the Twelve.

Yaldabaoth is Ashamed
11.5: And having witnessed the likeness of Pistis in the waters, the Primal Parent sorrowed greatly, especially when he heard her voice, which resembled the first voice that had called to him from out of the waters, and he moaned when he became aware that this was she who had bestowed on him a name. He was ashamed over his sin, and when he came to know truly that a deathless man of light had been in existence before him, he was deeply troubled, because previously he had announced to all the gods and to their angels, “I am the one who is God. Except me there is nothing else that exists,” because he had feared they could discover that someone else had existed before he had, and they might denounce him.
11.6: He, however, lacking discernment, laughed at (the possibility of) denunciation, and behaved rashly. He said, “If

12.1:
[ 108 ] something existed before I did, let it come forth, so we might behold its light,” and straightaway, behold! Light came forth from out of the eighth heaven above, and passed through all of the heavens of the earth.

Adam of Light
12.2: When the Primal Parent saw that the light was beautiful as it was glowing, he was astonished, and he grew deeply ashamed. As that light came forth, a quite wondrous human likeness manifested itself inside it, and no one saw it apart from the Primal Parent and Pronoia, who dwelt with him. Nevertheless, its light manifested itself to all the hosts of the heavens, on account of which all of them were troubled.
12.3: When Pronoia then saw that messenger, she fell in love with him, but he loathed her because she dwelt in darkness, yet she wanted to embrace him, and she could not. When she could not quench her love, she poured out her light onto the earth. From that day, that messenger has been called “Adam of Light,” which in translation means, “the radiant man of blood,” and the earth was spread out above him, the holy Adaman, which in translation means, “the Holy Land of the Adamantine.”
12.4: From that day, every authority has honored the blood of the virgin, and the earth was purified on account of the blood of the virgin, but additionally, the water was purified by means of the likeness of Pistis Sophia, who had appeared to the Primal Parent inside the waters. Consequently, rightly it has been said, “(it appeared) through the waters.” Because it gives life to everything,

13.1:
[ 109 ] the holy water purifies everything.

Eros
13.2: As an androgynous entity, Eros appeared from out of that primal blood. His masculine element is Himireris, which is fire from light. His feminine element that dwells together with him, a soul consisting of blood, originates from the substance of Pronoia. He is quite lovely in his beauty, possessing a charm surpassing all the created entities of Chaos.
13.3: All the gods then, and their angels, when they gazed on Eros, fell in love with him, and manifesting himself inside of all of them, he set them ablaze, just like several lamps are lit from a single lamp, even one and the same light is present, yet the lamp is not diminished, and in this way Eros dispersed himself inside all of the created entities of Chaos, and was not diminished. Just like Eros appeared at the center of light and darkness, and (just like) the sexual union of Eros was consummated at the center of the angels and humanity, so from out of the earth the primal pleasure bloomed. Woman followed Earth; marriage followed Woman. Birth followed marriage; decline followed birth.
13.4: After Eros, the grapevine sprouted up from out of that blood shed onto the earth. On account of this, those who imbibe it generate desire for sexual union.
13.5: After the grapevine, a fig tree as well as a pomegranate tree sprouted up from the earth, together with the remainder of the trees, every species, possessing their seed from the

14.1:
[ 110 ] seed of the authorities and of their angels.

Paradise
14.2: Justice next created Paradise. It was beautiful and lay outside the orbit of the moon and the orbit of the sun, inside the Land of Delight, in the east among the stones, and desire dwells among the beautiful, satisfying trees, and the tree of eternal life appeared, in accord with the will of God, to the north of Paradise, in order that the souls of the saints could become deathless, those who shall emerge from the lowly shaped forms at the consummation of the age. The color of the tree of life resembles the sun, and its branches are lovely. Its leaves resemble those of the cypress. Its fruit resembles a cluster of grapes when white. Its height reaches up to heaven, and beside it (is) the tree of knowledge, possessing the strength of God. Its glory resembles the moon when it is in full light, and its branches are lovely. Its leaves resemble fig leaves. Its fruit resembles a good, satisfying date, and this tree is to the north of Paradise, in order that it could shake souls from the lethargy of the demons, in order that they could draw near to the tree of life, and eat of its fruit, and in this way denounce the authorities and their angels.
14.3: The impact of this tree is detailed in holy Scripture, namely: “You are the tree of knowledge, which is in Paradise, from which the first man ate, and which opened his mind, and he loved his female companion, and denounced

15.1: [ 111 ] the other alien likenesses, even despising them.”
15.2:
After this, the olive tree sprouted up to sanctify kings and high priests of righteousness, who were to appear in the last days, given that the olive tree appeared from out of the light of the first Adam to supply the anointing they were to obtain.

The Creation of Plants and Animals
15.3: And primal Psyche loved Eros, who dwelt with her, and poured her blood onto himself as well as onto the earth, and from out of that blood the first rose sprouted up from out of the earth, coming out of the thorn bush, as a source of gladness for the light that was to appear from within the bush.
15.4: Additionally, after this the lovely flowers of pleasant aroma sprouted up from the earth, of different varieties, from each of the virgin daughters of Pronoia, and when they had fallen in love with Eros, they poured out their blood onto him and onto the earth.
15.5: After these, all the plants sprouted up from the earth, of different varieties, bearing inside of them the seed of the authorities and of their angels.
15.6: After these, from out of the waters the authorities created different varieties of animal species, including reptiles and birds, bearing inside of them the seed of the authorities and their angels.
15.7:
However, before all of these, when he had appeared on the first day, he lingered on earth approximately two days, and departed from the lower Pronoia in heaven, and ascended towards his light, and straightaway darkness obscured the entire cosmos.

The Creation of Heavenly Bodies

16.1: [ 112 ] As she desired, the Sophia who dwelt in the lower heaven obtained authority from Pistis, and she formed large shining bodies, and every star, and she placed them in the sky in order to shine on the earth, and to determine temporal signs, and seasons, and years, and months, and days, and nights, and minutes, and so on, and thus was adorned the whole area on the sky.
16.2: Now, when Adam of Light conceived the desire to enter into his light, namely, the eighth heaven, he could not do it on account of the poverty that had mingled together with his light. He then created an immense aeon for himself, and inside that aeon he created six aeons, and their adornments, numbering six, which were seven times superior to the heavens of Chaos and their adornments.
16.3: Now all these aeons and their adornments subsist inside the infinity that lies between the eighth heaven and the Chaos beneath it, being counted together with the universe that belongs to poverty.
16.4:
If you wish to learn their structure, you will find it written in the Seventh World of the Prophet Hieralias.

The Creation of the Man
16.5: And prior to Adam of Light retreating inside the Chaos, the authorities noticed him and mocked the Primal Parent because he had lied (to them) when he said: “I am the one who is God. No one existed before me.”
16.6: When they approached him, they asked: “Is this not the god who spoiled our work?”
16.7: He answered and said: “Yes. If you want him to be unable to spoil our work, come, let us create a man out of earth to serve us, according to the image of our body, and according to the likeness

17.1: [ 113 ] of this being, so that when he beholds his (own) likeness, he will fall in love with it. He will spoil our work no more. We will instead make servants for us of those who are born from out of the light for the entire duration of this aeon.”
17.2: All of this transpired in accord with the forethought of Pistis, so that (the) man would appear after his likeness, and would denounce them on account of their shaped form, and their shaped form became a place enclosing the light.
17.3: The authorities then obtained the knowledge requisite for creating (the) man. Sophia Zoe, she who dwells together with Sabaoth, had foreseen what they would do, and she mocked their decision, because they are blind. Contradicting their own (self-)interests, in ignorance they created him, and they did not understand what they were about to undertake.
17.4: She anticipated them and made her own man first. This was so that he could inform the form they had shaped how to hate them, and in this way to escape from them.
17.5: The teacher was produced in the following way. When Sophia allowed a droplet of light to descend, it flowed onto the water, and straightaway an androgynous human appeared. She shaped that droplet first as a female body. Making use of the body, she afterwards shaped it into the likeness of the mother, who had (previously) appeared, and she completed it within twelve months.
17.6: An androgynous human had been produced, whom the Greeks call Hermaphrodites, and whose mother the Hebrews call Eve of Zoe, that is, the female teacher of life. Her child is the created entity who is lord. The authorities afterwards

18.1:
[ 114 ] called it “the Beast,” so that it could lead astray the created entities that had shaped. The interpretation of “the Beast” is “the Teacher,” because it was found to be the cleverest of all beings.

Eve
18.2: Eve is the first virgin, the one who apart from a husband bore her first child. She is the one who served as her own midwife, on account of which she is considered to have said:
18.3: I am the one who is the part of my mother, and I am the one who is the mother. I am the one who is the wife; I am the one who is the virgin. I am the one who is pregnant; I am the one who is the midwife. I am the one who eases the pains of travail. My husband is the one who gave birth to me, and I am the one who is his mother, and he is the one who is my father, and my lord. He is the one who is my strength. Whatever he wishes, he speaks with reason. I am on the way to becoming, Although (already) I have given birth to a man as a lord.
18.4:
Now these things were disclosed by the will of Sabaoth and his Christ to the souls that were to enter into the shaped forms of the authorities, and of these the holy voice said, “Multiply and flourish, rule over all created entities,” and they were the ones who were taken captive, in accord with their destinies, by the Primal Parent, and in this way they were locked up inside the prisons of the shaped forms <. . .> until the consummation of the age.

The Seven Archons Fashion Adam
18.5: Then the Primal Parent next delivered an opinion regarding the man to those who dwelt with him. Each one of them then cast his sperm into the center of the navel of the earth.
18.6: From that day, the seven archons have fashioned man together with his body to resemble their (own) body, yet his likeness resembles the man who had appeared to them. His shaping occurred one part at a time, and their leader formed the brain as well as the nervous system.
18.7: He appeared afterwards like the one who was prior to him. He became

19.1: [ 115 ] a man possessing a soul, and he was called Adam, that is, “Father,” in accord with the name of the one who had existed prior to him, and when they had completed Adam, he forsook him like a lifeless vessel, given that he had taken on form like an abortion, without a spirit inside him.
19.2: When the chief archon recalled the speech of Pistis, he feared in case the true man might enter into his shaped form and become its lord. This is why for forty days he departed from his shaped form, which (then) lacked a soul, and he retreated and forsook it.
19.3: On the fortieth day, Sophia Zoe sent her breath into Adam, who was without soul. He began to move on the ground, and he was unable to stand erect.
19.4: Next, when the seven archons arrived, they saw him, and became deeply troubled. They approached him, and seized him, and he spoke to the breath inside him: “Who are you? And from where did you come to here?”
19.5: It answered, and said: “I have come from the force of the man in order to ruin your work.” Upon hearing this, they glorified him, because he granted them respite from the fear and the apprehension in which they found themselves.
19.6:
They then called that day “Rest,” because they had rested from work, and when they saw that Adam was able to stand erect, they rejoiced, and they took him and placed him inside Paradise, and they retreated up to their heavens.

Eve Gives Life to Adam
19.7:
After the day of rest, Sophia dispatched her daughter Zoe, called Eve, as a teacher, so that she could make the soulless Adam stand up, so that those whom he would beget could become vessels of light.

[When]

20.1: [ 116 ] Eve saw her male companion lying prostrate, she had compassion on him, and she said: “Adam, live! Stand up on the earth!”
20.2: Her utterance straightaway was fulfilled in act, because Adam, after standing up, speedily opened his eyes. When he beheld her, he said: “You will be called ‘Mother of the Living,’ because you are the one who has given me life.”
20.3: The Authorities and their Angels Assault the Likeness of Eve
20.4: It was then reported to the authorities that their shaped form was alive and had stood up, and they were deeply disturbed. They dispatched seven archangels to learn what had transpired.
20.5: They approached Adam. When they saw Eve speaking with him, they said to each other: “What kind of entity is this radiant woman? Because she is similar to that likeness which manifested itself to us inside the light. Come now, let us seize her and cast our seed into her, so that when she is defiled she will be unable to ascend into her light. Instead, those she gives birth to will be at our command. However, let us not inform Adam, because he is not one of us. Instead, let us put a profound sleep over him, and let us teach him while he is asleep how she originated from his rib, so that his wife will obey, and he will be lord over her.”
20.6: Because she was a force, Eve then laughed at their decision. She made mist enter into their eyes, and covertly left her likeness with Adam.
20.7: She entered into the tree of knowledge and lingered there, and they chased after her, and she disclosed to them that she had entered into the tree, and had become a tree. Falling then into a great fear, the blind entities escaped.
20.8: When afterwards they had shaken off the stupor, they approached Adam, and seeing the likeness of this woman

21.1: [ 117 ] together with him, they were deeply troubled, believing that she was the actual Eve, and they behaved impulsively. They approached her, and seized her, and cast their seed onto her.
21.2: They committed this in evil, defiling with natural and obscene means, first defiling the seal of her voice, which had spoken with them, saying: “What existed before you?” (In this way they) meant to defile at the consummation (of the age) those who might declare that they were born of the true man by means of verbal articulation, and they went astray, being unaware that they had defiled their own body, it being the likeness the authorities and their angels defiled with every means.
21.3: The Offspring of the Archon, the Authorities, and their Angels
21.4: She first became pregnant with Abel, by the first archon, and by the seven authorities and their angels she had the other children, and everything transpired in agreement with the forethought of the Primal Parent, in order that the Primal Mother could bear every seed inside her, being mixed and joined to the destiny of the universe and its structures, and a plan designed beforehand by Justice was set in motion regarding Eve, namely, that the shaped forms of the authorities would become places to enclose the light, at which it would censure them through their shaped forms.
21.5: The Primal Adam, of Light, is imbued with spirit, and he appeared on the first day. The second Adam is imbued with soul, and he appeared on the sixth day, called “Aphrodite.” The third Adam is a created entity of the earth, namely, the man of the Law, and he appeared on the eighth day, called “Sun-Day,” [following]

22.1:
[ 118 ] the lowly Rest-Day, and the descendants of the earthly Adam multiplied and filled the earth, and from inside them they made all kinds of technological skills possessed by the Adam imbued with soul. However, all of them dwelt in ignorance.

The Tree of Knowledge
22.2: Allow me to say next that once the archons had witnessed him and the female being who dwelt with him going astray unawares like beasts, they were extremely happy.
22.3: Upon learning that the deathless man would not ignore them, they grew upset that they instead would have to be afraid of the female being who had turned herself into a tree, and they said: “Maybe this is the real man, this being who put a mist over us, and who taught us that she who had been defiled resembles him, and then we will be defeated.”
22.4: Then together these seven concocted schemes together. They nervously approached Adam and Eve, saying to him: “The fruit of any of the trees created for you in Paradise may be eaten, but regarding the tree of knowledge, exercise self-constraint, and do not eat of it. If you do eat, you will die.” After creating deep anxiety inside them, they retreated up to their authorities.
22.5: The cleverest of all creatures then approached, called “Beast,” and when he had beheld the likeness of their mother Eve, he said to her: “What has God said to you? Was it, ‘Eat not of the tree of knowledge’?”
22.6: She said: “Not only did he say, ‘Eat not of it,’ but, ‘Touch it not, or you will die.’”
22.7: He said to her: “Fear not, with death you will not die, because he knows that when you eat

23.1: [ 119 ] of it, your reasoning will grow sober, and you will become as gods, knowing the difference between evil and good humans. In fact, he said this to you with jealously, to make you not eat of it.”
23.2:
Eve now possessed confidence in the sayings of the teacher. She observed the tree and recognized that it was beautiful and satisfying, and she liked it. She took some of its fruit, and ate of it, and she also gave some to her husband, and he also ate of it. Their mind then was opened, because upon eating, the light of knowledge had shone on them. When they had clothed themselves with embarrassment, they realized they were naked without knowledge. When they sobered up, they realized they were naked, and they fell in love with each other. When they realized that the ones who had shaped them had the shape of beasts, they hated them. They had become acutely aware.

The Archons Curse Eve, Adam, and All Creation
23.3: When the archons then realized that (Adam and Eve) had broken their commandments (to them), they arrived in Paradise and approached Adam and Eve, accompanied by an earthquake and big threats, to see the result of their support. Adam and Eve then shook violently and hid beneath the trees in Paradise. The archons then were unaware of where they were, and said: “Adam, where are you?”
23.4: He said: “Here I am, because out of fear of you I hid, being embarrassed,” and they said to him in ignorance: “Who informed you of the embarrassment with which you have clothed yourself, unless you have eaten from that tree?”
23.5:
He said: “The woman you gave to me, she is the one who gave to me, and I ate.”

They said then to the latter:

24.2: She answered, and said: “The teacher is the one who incited, and I ate.”
24.3: The archons then approached the teacher. Their eyes grew foggy on account of him, and they were unable to do anything against him. They cursed him, given that they were powerless.
24.4: After this, they approached the woman and cursed her as well as her descendants.
24.5: After the woman, they cursed Adam, as well as the land, on account of him, the crops also, and they cursed everything they had created. They possess no blessing. Good cannot be the consequence of evil.
24.6: From that day, the authorities truly realized there was something more powerful than they.
24.7: They knew only that their commandments had not been observed. A tremendous jealousy was introduced into the world solely on account of the deathless man.
24.8: When the archons realized that their Adam had gained a different kind of knowledge, they wanted to put him to the test, and they assembled together every tame animal and the wild beasts of the earth, as well as the birds of heaven, and brought them in front of Adam, in order to learn what he would call them. When he had seen them, he assigned names to their creatures.
24.9: They grew disturbed on account of Adam recovering from every test. They gathered and concocted schemes, and they said: “Behold Adam! He has become like one of us, in that he knows the difference between light and darkness. Perhaps now he will be fooled, as is the case with the tree of knowledge, and will even approach the tree of life, and eat of it, and become deathless, and become lord, and loathe us and despise us, as well as all of our glory. He will then condemn us together with our universe. Come, let us banish him

25.1: [ 121 ] from Paradise, down to the earth from where he was taken, in order that from now on he will be unable to know anything superior to what we are capable of.” And in this way, they banished Adam from Paradise, together with his wife, and this act they perpetrated was not sufficient for them. Instead, they grew fearful.
25.2: They entered (Paradise, approaching) the tree of life, and enclosed it with large fearsome entities, fiery living creatures called “Cherubin,” and they placed a flaming sword among them, fearsomely rotating continuously, to prevent any earthly being ever entering that place.
25.3:
Given that the archons grew jealous of Adam, they desired to shorten their lifespans. They were unable, on account of fate, which had been set from the beginning, because to each one a lifespan of 1,000 years had been assigned, in agreement with the orbit of the radiant bodies. However, even though the archons were unable to accomplish this, each one of the perpetrators of evil subtracted ten years, and the full lifespan reached to 930 years, and these pass in suffering, and feebleness, and malevolent disruption, and this is the way life has been, from that day, until the consummation of the age.

Sophia Zoe
25.4:
So, when Sophia Zoe witnessed the archons of the darkness putting a curse on her companions, she grew furious, and exiting the first heaven with plenary power, she hounded those archons, ejecting them from out of [their] heavens, and threw them down into the world of transgression, to make them dwell there in the form of wicked demons on the earth.

[She dispatched a bird],

26.1: [ 122 ] which in their world would spend its thousand years in Paradise, a living creature imbued with soul, called “phoenix.” It dies by suicide and revivifies itself, in order to be a witness to the judgment (decreed) against them, because they mistreated Adam and his race, even to the consummation of the age.
26.2: There are three men, as well as their descendants, to the consummation of the world: those imbued with spirit, and those imbued with soul, and the earthly. Similarly, the three phoenixes <inside> Paradise: the first is deathless, the second lives for 1,000 years. Of the third it is written in the sacred Scripture that it is consumed. Similarly, as well, there are three baptisms: the first is spiritual, the second is with fire, the third is with water.
26.3: Precisely as the phoenix symbolizes the angels, so is the case of the water hydri in Egypt, which symbolizes those who descend into the baptism of a true man.
26.4: The two bulls in Egypt possess a symbolic meaning, namely, the sun and moon, which is a symbol of Sabaoth, on account of Sophia obtaining the universe from the day that she fashioned the sun and the moon, placing a seal on her heaven, until the age ends.
26.5: And the worm born out of the phoenix is also symbolic of a human being, of which it is written, “the just man will blossom like a phoenix,” and the phoenix appears first alive, and dies, and rises again, functioning as a symbol of what will happen at the consummation of the age.
26.6: These powerful symbols appeared solely in Egypt, not elsewhere, to indicate

27.1:
[ 123 ] that it resembles the Paradise of God.

The Seven Archons and their Demonic Angels
27.2: Let us return to the archons we discussed previously, so we can offer an explanation of them.
27.3: When the seven archons had been thrown down from out of their heavens onto the earth, they fashioned for themselves copious demonic angels in order to serve them, and these latter taught humanity several kinds of error, and magic, and potions, and idol worship, and bloodshed, and altars, and temples, and sacrifices, and libations to all the earthly demons, collaborating together with fate, who came into being from the agreement between the gods of injustice and justice, and in this way, when the world had come to be, it went astray, continually confused, because all humans on earth worshiped demons, from the creation to the consummation (of the age), both the angels of righteousness and the humans of unrighteousness.
27.4: In this way, the world had come to exist in confusion, in ignorance, and in a stupor. All of them had gone astray, until the appearance of the true man.
27.5:
Let this be sufficient as far as the topic is concerned.

The Deathless Man
27.6: Now we will move on to consider our world, so that we can with precision complete the description of its structure and governance. It will then become clear how faithfulness to the unseen aeon was found, which has been manifest from creation until the consummation of the age.
27.7: Consequently, I arrive at the chief themes concerning the deathless man. I will discuss the beings that pertain to him, showing how it is that they are here.
27.8: When a multitude of humans had come into existence, by the parentage of [the Adam who]

28.1: [ 124 ] had been made, even from out of matter, and when the world had already become fully populated, the archons were its master; that is, they maintained its bondage with ignorance. And why? For the following reason: Given that the deathless father is aware that a deficiency in truth came to exist among the aeons and their universe, when he desired to bring to nullity the archons of perdition by means of the creatures they had shaped, he dispatched your likenesses down into the world of perdition, that is, the blessed small spirits of innocence. They are not strangers to knowledge, because all of knowledge is lodged in a single angel who appeared to them. He does not lack power in the presence of the father, even for <him> to give them knowledge. When they appear in the world of perdition, they straightaway reveal the structure of indestructibility as a censure of the archons and their hosts.
28.2: In this way, when the blessed entities appeared in forms shaped by the authorities, they were envied, and out of envy the authorities joined their seed together with theirs, wishing to defile them. They were incapable of this.
28.3: When then the blessed entities appeared in a radiant form, they appeared in several modes, and they originated from different aeons, revealing their knowledge to the church made visible by the shaped forms of perdition. She was found to contain every kind of seed, on account of the seed of the authorities that had been joined [with her].
28.4: The savior then created all of them [(as) one], and their spirits are clearly superior, being blessed

29.1: [ 125 ] and variously chosen, as well as several other beings having no king and being superior to all those who existed before they had.
29.2: Four races therefore exist, three pertaining to the kings of the eighth heaven, but the fourth race being kingless, even perfect, which is the highest of them all, because these are the ones who will enter into the Holy Place of their father, and they will obtain rest together with repose, and eternal, ineffable glory, and infinite joy.
29.3:
What is more, they are kings inside the realm of death, given that they are deathless. They will censure the gods of Chaos and their hosts.

The Logos
29.4: The all-superior Logos was dispatched solely for this reason: that he could announce the unknown. He said, “Nothing that is hidden is not revealed, and what is unknown will be known,” and these were dispatched to make known what is hidden, even the seven authorities of Chaos as well as their impiety, and in this way they were sentenced to death.
29.5:
When all the perfect ones appeared in the forms shaped by the archons, and when they revealed the truth beyond compare, they humiliated all the wisdom of the gods, and their fate was found to be a censure, and their host withered away. Their lordship dissipated. Their forethought became nothing, together with their glory.

The Consummation of the Age
29.6: Before the consummation of the age, the entire place will tremble with loud thunder. The archons will then grow sorrowful over [fear of] their (impending)

30.1: [ 126 ] death. The angels will lament for their humanity, and the demons will weep over their seasons, and their humanity will moan and shriek at their (impending) death.
30.2: The age will then begin, and they will become troubled. Their kings will become inebriated with the fiery sword, and they will wage war against each other, causing the earth to be drunk with bloodshed, and the seas will be troubled by those wars. The sun will then grow dark, and the moon will eclipse its light. The stars of the sky will stop following their circuits, and a loud thunder blast will emerge from out of a great host that is over every host of Chaos, where the firmament of the woman is located.
30.3: After having produced the first creation, she will lay aside the wise fire of reasoning and clothe herself with unreasoning wrath.
30.4: She will next hound the gods of Chaos, whom she created together with the Primal Parent. She will thrust them down into the Abyss. They will be annihilated for their evil, because they will become like volcanoes, and devour each other until they are destroyed by the power of the Primal Parent.
30.5: After destroying them, he will turn against himself, even destroying himself until he no longer exists, and their heavens will fall on each other, and their hosts will be devoured by fire. Their aeons will be overthrown as well, and his heaven will plummet and shatter in two. His [stars . . .] will plummet onto the earth, [and the earth will be unable] to endure them. They will plummet into the Abyss, and the Abyss will be overthrown. The light will [conquer] the darkness and annihilate it. It will become like

31.1: [ 127 ] something that never existed, and the origin of darkness will dissipate, and the deficiency will be uprooted, thrown down into the darkness, and the light will retreat upwards to its root, and the glory of the unbegotten one will appear, and it will fill every aeon when the prophecies and the writings of kings are revealed and fulfilled by those who are called perfect.
31.2:
Those, however, who have not become perfect in the unbegotten Father will obtain their glory in their aeons and in the kingdoms of the deathless ones, but they will never enter the kingless aeon, because each must go to the place from which he came. By his deeds and his knowledge, each will reveal his (respective) nature.

Notes
31.9: There is no need to emend the text here.
31.12: “Primal pleasure,” I borrow the wording from the Bethge/Layton translation.
31.14: This is a targumic-like paraphrase of various verses from Genesis 2 and 3.
31.15: “Seal of her voice.” This seems to refer to her physical mouth.

1.1:
The Fall of the Soul

[ 127 ] Long ago sages gave the soul a feminine name. She is in fact also female in her nature. She even has a womb.
1.2: For as long as she dwelt in solitude with the Father, she was virgin, and in form she was androgynous. When she, however, fell into a body and entered this life, she then fell into the hands of many robbers. And the cruel creatures passed her between each other and [violated] her. Some used her forcefully, while others seduced her with a gift. To be brief, they defiled her, and she [lost] her

2.1: [ 128 ] virginity.
2.2: And in her body she practiced prostitution and gave herself to all without exception, thinking of each one she was ready to embrace as her husband. When she had surrendered herself to cruel, faithless adulterers, so they could misuse her, she then moaned profoundly and repented.
2.3: Yet even when she turned away her face from those adulterers, she ran to others, and they forced her to live with them and to be of service to them on their bed, as though they were her masters. Ashamed, she stopped daring to leave them. They, for their part, tricked her for a long time, posing as loyal, true husbands, as though they greatly reverenced her. And after all this, they forsook her and went away.
2.4: Next she became a helpless, poor, desolate widow. In the time of her distress, not a morsel of food was left for her. All she ever gained from them was the sullying that came from sexual intercourse. And her children from the adulterers are dumb, blind, ailing, and weak-minded.
2.5: When, however, the exalted Father visited her and looked on her, and saw her moaning in her pains and shame, repenting for the prostitution she practiced, and when she started to invoke his name that he might help her, [she moaned] with all her heart and said: “Save me, my Father. Look on me, because I will give [an account to you], because I forsook my house and

3.1: [ 129 ] escaped from my maiden’s quarters. Restore me to yourself once more.”
3.2:
When he beholds her in this condition, he will then consider her worthy of bestowing his mercy on her, because many are the sufferings that befell her because she forsook her house.

The Prostitution of the Soul according to the Scriptures
3.3: Now, regarding the prostitution of the soul, the Holy Spirit prophesies in many places, saying in the prophet Jeremiah:
3.4:
If a husband divorces his wife and she goes and takes another man, can she go back to him again? Has not that woman completely polluted herself? “And you played the harlot to many shepherds and you returned to me,” said the Lord. “Take a clear look and see where you played the harlot. Were you not sitting in the streets polluting the land with your harlotries and your wickedness? And you took many shepherds as a stumbling block to you. With everyone you were without shame. You called not on me as a relative or as father or guardian of your virginity.” (Jeremiah 3:1-4)

Again, it is written in the prophet Hosea:
3.5: “Come, go to court with your mother, for she will not be a wife to me, and I will not be a husband to her. I shall take away her harlotry from before me, and I shall take away her adultery from between her breasts. I shall strip her naked as on the day she was born, and I shall make her a wilderness like a waterless land, and I shall make her [yearn in childlessness]. I will not have compassion on her children, for they are children of harlotry, because their mother played the harlot and [acted shamefully to her children].

4.1:
[ 130 ] For she said, ‘I shall play the harlot to my lovers. They gave me my bread and my water, and my vesture and my garments, and my wine and my oil, and everything I had need of.’ Behold, therefore, I shall close them in so that she cannot run after her lovers. And when she seeks them but does not find them, she will say, ‘I shall go back to my former husband; I was better off then than now.’” (Hosea 2:2-7)

Again, he says in Ezekiel:
4.2: “It came to pass after much wickedness,” said the Lord, “you built a brothel and you made a place for your beauty in the streets. And you built brothels on every street, and you squandered your beauty, and you spread your legs in every alley, and you multiplied your acts of harlotry. You played the harlot to the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, men great of flesh.” (Ezekiel 16:23-26)
4.3: What, however, does “the sons of Egypt, men great of flesh” mean, except the kingdom of the flesh and the perceptible realm and earthly affairs, which sully the soul here, obtaining bread from them, and wine besides, and oil, garments, and further senseless external things around the body, things she believes are necessary for her?
4.4: Regarding this prostitution, however, the apostles of the Savior insisted: “Guard yourselves from it; purify yourselves from it.” This pertains not only to bodily prostitution, but especially of the soul. For this cause the apostles write [to the churches] of God, so that [this kind (of prostitution)] might not happen among us.
4.5: Nevertheless, the most difficult [challenge] pertains to the prostitution

5.1: [ 131 ] of the soul. From it originates also bodily prostitution. Therefore Paul, writing to the Corinthians, said, “I wrote you in the letter, ‘Do not associate with prostitutes,’ not at all (referring to) the prostitutes of this world or the greedy or robbers or idolaters, because then you would need to leave the world.” (1 Corinthians 5:9-10). In this case he is speaking spiritually, “For our struggle is not against flesh and blood,” as he said, “but against the world rulers of this darkness and the spirits of wickedness.” (Ephesians 6:12)
5.2:
For as long as the soul continues running around everywhere, having sex with everyone she meets and sullying herself, she suffers what she deserves.

The Restoration of the Soul
5.3: When, however, she realizes the trouble she is in and cries before the Father and repents, the Father then will show mercy to her. And he will cause her womb to turn away from the outward kingdom, and will cause it to return inward, making the soul reclaim her good character. Because such is not the way of a woman, for the bodily womb is inward, like the other internal organs of the body.
5.4: The womb of the soul, however, surrounds outwardly like the male’s outward genitals. When, therefore, the womb of the soul turns inward by the will of the Father, it is baptized and immediately purified from the outward pollution which was forced on it, like filthy [garments] soaked [in water and] moved around until the dirt is gone and they are clean. Thus the purification of the soul is a reclaiming of the renovation of

6.1: [ 132 ] her former nature, and a return to herself. That is her baptism.
6.2: Then she will become mad at herself, acting like a woman during labor, writhing and raging in the hour of birth. However, because she is a female, on her own she is unable to conceive a child. From heaven the Father sent her a man – her brother, the firstborn. The bridegroom then went down to the bride. She stopped her earlier prostitution and purified herself from the pollutions of the adulterers. She was even renewed to become a bride. She purified herself in the bridal chamber, filling it with perfume, sitting there awaiting her true bridegroom. She no longer ran around the marketplace, having sex with everyone she wanted. Instead, she kept waiting for him: “When will he arrive?” And she continued to fear him, because she knew not what he looked like. She no more remembered the time she fell from her Father’s house. By the will of the father, however, [. . .] And she dreamed of him like a woman who loves a man.
6.3:
Then, however, the bridegroom, agreeing with the Father’s will, went down to her, into the bridal chamber, which had been prepared, and he adorned the bridal chamber.

The Marriage of the Soul
6.4: Because that marriage is unlike carnal marriage, those who will have sex with each other will be content with that kind of sex. And, as though it were a weight, they leave behind them the bother of bodily lust, [turning away their faces] from each other. This marriage, however, [is different]. When, however, they have joined [with one another], they become one life.

7.1: [ 133 ] Because of this the prophet said about the first man and the first woman, “They will become one flesh.” (Genesis 2:24)
7.2: For they were at first joined to each other when they dwelt with the Father before the woman led astray the man who is her brother. This marriage has joined them together again, and the soul has been united with her true love, her original master; as it is written, “For the woman’s master is her husband.” (Genesis 3:16; Ephesians 5:23)
7.3:
One step at a time she then recognized him, and she rejoiced again, weeping in his presence, recalling her earlier shame as a widow. And she beautified herself even more so that he would be delighted to abide with her.

And the prophet said in the Psalms:
7.4: Hear, my daughter, and look, and incline your ear, and forget your people and your father’s house, and the king will desire your beauty, for he is your lord.” (Psalm 45:10-11)
7.5: For he commands her to turn her gaze away from her people and from the crowd of her adulterers, among whom she once dwelt, to dedicate herself to her king alone, her true Lord, and to forget her earthly father’s house, where the situation was appalling for her, and instead to remember her Father who is in heaven.
7.6: Accordingly, it was also said to Abraham: “Go from your country and your kindred and from your father`s house.” (Genesis 12:1)
7.7: In this way, after the soul [had beautified] herself once more in her splendor, [she desired] to adore her beloved, and [he, too], loved her. And when she united with him, she obtained

8.1: [ 134 ] from him the seed of the life-giving spirit. By it she bears upright children and raises them, because this is the great, perfect miracle of birth. And so this marriage is completed by the will of the Father.
8.2: It is appropriate that the soul regenerates herself and again becomes what she earlier was. The soul then moves by her own will, and from the Father she obtains the divine nature for her renewal, to restore her to the place where she was at first:
8.3:
This is the resurrection from the dead. This is redemption from slavery. This is the rising journey of ascent to heaven. This is the path of ascent to the father.

The prophet, therefore, said:
8.4: Praise the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, praise his holy name. My soul, praise God, who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases, who ransoms your life from death, who crowns you with mercy, who satisfies your longing with good things. Your youth will be renewed like the eagle’s. (Psalm 103:1-5)
8.5:
After she is young again, she will ascend, praising the Father and her brother who saved her. In this way, by being born again, the soul is saved. And this is not by repeating formulas or by educated expertise or by learning from books. It is instead by the grace of the [Spirit]; it is the gift of the compassionate [God]. This is the way of this heavenly reality.

The Savior therefore calls out:

9.1:
[ 135 ] “No one can come to me unless my Father draws him and brings him to me; and I will raise him up on the last day.” (John 6:44)

Repentance
9.2:
And so it is appropriate to pray to the Father and to invoke him with all our soul, sighing, not outwardly with the lips, but with the inward spirit that comes from the depth, repenting the former life we led, confessing our sins, understanding the vacuous lie we lived in, and the hollow zealotry, wailing because of the darkness and the wave that engulfed us, weeping for ourselves so that he would show us compassion, hating ourselves because of what we are now.

The Savior again said:
9.3: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be pitied. Blessed are those who are hungry, for they will be filled.” (Matthew 5:4,6; Luke 6:21)
9.4: He said once more, “If one does not hate his soul he cannot follow me.” (Luke 14:26)
9.5: This is because the beginning of salvation is repentance. And so, “Before Christ appeared, John came, preaching the baptism of repentance.” (Acts 13:24)
9.6: And repentance occurs in pain and sorrow. The Father, however, is good and loves humanity, and he listens to the soul who calls on him, sending it the light of salvation. By the Spirit he therefore said to the prophet:
9.7: Say to the children of my people: “[If] your sins reach [from earth to] heaven, and if they are [red] as scarlet, and blacker than sackcloth, [and if]

10.1: [ 136 ] you return to me with all your soul, and say to me ‘my Father!’ I will listen to you as a holy people.” ( 1 Clement 8:3)
10.2:
Yet another passage: “Thus says the Lord, the holy one of Israel: ‘If you return and weep, then you will be saved, and you will know where you were when you hoped in what is empty.’” (Isaiah 30:15)

And in another passage, he said:
10.3: Jerusalem wept much, saying, “Have pity on me.” He will be gracious to you at the sound of your weeping. And when he saw, he answered you. And the Lord will give you bread of adversity and water of affliction. From now on, those who lie to you will not approach you again. Your eyes will see those who lie to you. (Isaiah 30:19-20)
10.4:
And so it is appropriate to pray to God both night and day, spreading out our hands to him like those who sail in the middle of the sea. They pray to God with all their heart without duplicity, because those who pray with duplicity only lie to themselves. In fact, so that he might know who deserves salvation, God examines the inward parts and searches the depths of the heart. For no one who is still in love with the place of lies deserves salvation.

The Repentance of Odysseus and Helen

It is accordingly written in the poet:

11.1:
[ 137 ] it is to my home I would return. (Homer, Odyssey 4.260-261)

Because she moaned, saying:
11.2: It is Aphrodite who misled me and took me away from my village. My own daughter I forsook, and my husband, good, intelligent, handsome. (Homer, Odyssey 4.261-4.264)
11.3:
Because when the soul forsakes her perfect husband on account of the disloyalty of Aphrodite, who comes to exist here by the act of begetting, then she will come to injury. If however, she moans and repents, she will be returned to her house.

Conclusion
11.4:
Israel certainly would not have been visited in the beginning, to be rescued from the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, if it had not groaned to God and moaned over the tyranny of its slavery.

Again in the Psalms it is written:
11.5: I was greatly wearied by my groaning. I will flood my bed and my couch every night with my tears. I have grown old in the midst of all my enemies. Depart from me, all you workers of evil, for behold, the Lord has heard the cry of my weeping, and the Lord has accepted my prayer. (Psalm 6:6-9)
11.6:
If we repent, God will surely listen to us, he who is patient and richly merciful, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen!

The Exegesis on the Soul

1.1:
Incipit

[ 138 ] The secret sayings the Savior spoke to Judas Thomas that I, yes I, Mathaias, wrote down while I was walking, listening to them speak with one another.

The Savior Speaks with Thomas
1.2: The Savior said: “Brother Thomas, heed me while you have time (left) in the world, and I will disclose to you the things you have wondered about in your mind.
1.3:
“Because it has been said that you are my twin and true friend, study yourself and discover who you are, the mode in which you are, and how you will be (in the future). Because you will be called ‘my brother,’ it is not appropriate for you to be self-ignorant, yet I know you have comprehended (yourself), because you already comprehended that I am true knowledge. Thus, even though you do not comprehend, as you concur with me , you have already achieved knowledge, and (so) you will be called ‘the one of self-knowledge.’ This is because whoever has no self-knowledge is a know-nothing, but whoever has self-knowledge has together with it already obtained deep knowledge about everything. Consequently, my brother Thomas, you have gazed on what is veiled to humans, namely, what they in (self-)ignorance stumble over.”

The Visible and the Invisible
1.4: Thomas said to the Lord: “I implore you, then, to answer what I ask of you before your ascension, and when I hear from you about concealed things, that then I can discuss them (openly). And it is clear to me that it is difficult to do the truth in front of others.”
1.5: The Savior answered: “If visible things are concealed to you, how can you hear about invisible things? If it is difficult for you to do the works of truth that in this world are visible, then how, in fact, will you do those that relate to the invisible lofty height and Fullness? And how will you be called ‘workers’? In this regard you are students, and have not yet obtained the summit of perfection.”
1.6: Thomas responded and said to the Savior: “Explain to us about what you call invisible things, [that are nevertheless] concealed from us.”
1.7: The Savior said: [“All] bodies [. . .] the animals are begotten [. . .] it is manifest like [. . .] also this, those who are above [. . .] visible things, but [they are] visible

2.1: [ 139 ] in their own root, and their fruit nurtures them. These visible bodies, however, survive by eating animals that resemble them, the result being that the bodies change. What changes will degenerate and perish, and from that point on it loses any hope for life, because that is an animal body. Accordingly, just as animal bodies perish, so these (bodily) forms will also perish. They originate from intercourse, just like those of animals, no? If it also originates from intercourse, then how will it beget something different from the animals? Consequently, then, you will remain infants until you become mature.”
2.2: And Thomas responded: “I therefore tell you, Lord, that those who talk about invisible things and things difficult to interpret resemble those who at night shoot arrows at a target. They certainly shoot their arrows like everyone (else) who does, given that they shoot at the target, yet it cannot be seen. When, though, the light emerges and veils the darkness, the work of each will then appear. And O Lord, our light, illuminate us.”
2.3: Jesus said: “The nature of light is light.”
2.4: Thomas spoke: “Lord, why does this visible light that shines for humans rise and set?”
2.5:
The Savior responded: “O blessed Thomas, of course this visible light shines for you, not so that you will stay here, but so you can instead depart. And when all the chosen ones forsake the animal state, then this light will depart upward (back) to its essence, and it will greet (the light), because it is a good servant.”

Wisdom and Foolishness
2.6: The Savior continued then: “O unfathomable love of the light! O the bitterness of the fire burning in the bodies and marrow of humans, that by night and day is set ablaze in them, and that scorches the limbs of humans and [causes] their minds to become intoxicated and their souls to become insane [. . .] them in (both) males and females [. . .] night, and they perform movements, [. . .] in secret and in sight, because the males [perform movements . . . on the females] and the females on [the males]. [Accordingly, it is]

3.1: [ 140 ] said: ‘All those who look for the truth from true wisdom will grow wings for flying, escaping the lust that scorches human spirits, and will grow wings to escape any (evil) spirit they see.’”
3.2: And Thomas responded: “Lord, this is precisely what I ask you about, because I have comprehended that, as you say, you are our benefactor.”
3.3: The Savior answered again: “This is why we must speak to you, because this is the teaching for the mature. If you now want to become mature, you will fulfill these things. If you do not, your name is ‘Ignoramus,’ because whoever is intelligent cannot live with a fool, since whoever is intelligent is mature in all wisdom. Whoever is wise, in fact, will be nurtured by the truth and ‘will be like a tree growing by the winding stream.’ (Psalm 1:3) To the fool, though, good and evil are the same, considering that even though some possess wings, they nevertheless run to visible things that are distant from truth. The reason is the fire that guides them creates for them an illusion of truth, [and] it illuminates them with a [perishable] beauty, and it confines them in a sweet gloom and enchants them with aromatic indulgence.
3.4: “And it will blind them with an unquenchable lust, scorch their souls, and turn into something for them like a pole pounded into their heart that they will never be able to remove. And however it wishes, it drives them around like a bit in the mouth. And with the bitterness of the captivity of lust for visible things that on impulse degenerate, change, and deviate, it has bound them with its chains and fettered their every limb. They are ever being drawn downwards. When they are killed, they are digested by all the animals of the perishable realm.”
3.5: Thomas responded: “It is clear, even as it has been said, [‘Many are . . . those who know not] [. . .] soul.’”
3.6: And [the Savior] answered: [“Blessed is] the one who is wise, who [looked for the truth, and] when finding it,

4.1: [ 141 ] reposed on it forever and had no fear of those who sought to disturb him.”
4.2: Thomas responded: “Is it good for us, Lord, to repose among what pertains to us?”
4.3:
The Savior said: “Yes, it is helpful, and it is good for you, because things that are visible among humans will vanish, since their fleshly vessel will vanish, and when it is reduced to nothing, it will come to exist among visible things, among things that can be seen. And then the fire they see will cause them pain because of their former love for the faith. They will be regathered to what is visible. Furthermore, those who can see among invisible things, not possessing the greatest love, they will perish in their preoccupation over this life and the scorching of the fire. After but a little while, what is visible will vanish.Then formless shadows will come out, and among the graves they will linger forever on the corpses, suffering, and their soul in decay.”

The Day of Judgement
4.4: Thomas responded: “What can we say after these things? What can we say to the blind? What teaching should we communicate to these pitiable mortals who say: ‘We came here to [do] good and not to curse,’ and yet [say], ‘If we had not been begotten in the flesh, we would never have known [sin]’?”
4.5: The Savior said: “Truly, regarding [those], do not consider them as human, but consider them [as] animals, because just like animals eat each other, so this kind of people also eat each other. It is exactly the opposite; they have forfeited [the kingdom] with their love, the sweet fire, being slaves of death and running to (do) deeds of decay. They practice the lust of their ancestors. They will be cast down into the abyss to suffer the torment of the bitter evil of their nature, because they will be whipped, causing them to run backwards to where they cannot see, and they [will be separated] from their limbs, not (bearing it) bravely, but [in] despair. And they are glad because [. . .] insanity and irrationality [. . .] [They] chase after this irrationality without recognizing [their insanity, believing] that they [are] wise. [They . . .] their body [. . .]

5.1: [ 142 ] Their mind is selfishly oriented, because their thinking is preoccupied with their actions, but the fire will scorch them.”
5.2: And Thomas responded: “Lord, what will the person cast down to them do? Because I am very concerned for them, there being many who attack them.”
5.3: The Savior answered: “What do you yourself think?”
5.4: Judas, called Thomas, said: “Lord, it is right that you speak, and that I listen.”
5.5: The Savior responded: “Heed what I will tell you, and believe what is true. What sows and what is sown will vanish in the fire, in fire and water, and they will cover themselves in dark graves. And after a lot of time passes, they will manifest the fruit of evil trees, being reproved and killed in the mouths of animals and humans, urged on by the rains and winds and air and the light shining from above.”
5.6: Thomas responded: “Without a doubt you have convinced us, Lord. We know in our heart, and it is clear that it [is the case], and that your word suffices. These words you speak to us, however, are laughable and detestable to the world, because they are misinterpreted. So how can we go to preach them, because we are [not] respected [in] the world?”
5.7: The Savior responded: “I tell you truly that whoever hears [your] word and rejects it or mocks it or laughs at these matters, I tell you truly that he will be delivered to the ruler on high who as their king rules over every power, and he will twirl that one in circles and cast  him out from heaven down into the abyss, and he will be confined in a constricted gloomy place. Furthermore, he will be unable to turn or move because of the tremendous depth of Tartaros, and the [ponderous bitterness] of Hades that is unwavering. [. . .] them to it [. . .] they will not forgive [. . .] chase you. They will deliver [. . .] over to [. . .] angel Tartarouchos [. . .] fire chasing them.

6.1: [ 143 ] [. . .] fiery lashes that spew a shower of sparks into the face of the one being chased.
6.2: If he runs to the west, he will encounter the fire. If he runs to the south, he will encounter it there, too. If he turns to the north, the danger of boiling fire will meet him again. Nor can he find a way to the east to run away there and be rescued.
6.3:
Because he did not find it in the day when he dwelt in the body, he will not find it in the day of judgment.”

Condemnation of the Godless
6.4: The Savior then continued: “Woe to you who are godless, who are hopeless, expecting what will not come to pass! Woe to you whose hope is in the flesh, even in the prison bound to perish! How long will you be forgetful? And how long will you assume that imperishable things will also perish? Your hope is fixed on the world, your god being this life! You are destroying yourselves!
6.5: Woe to you inside the fire that scorches you inside, because it is unquenchable! Woe to you for of the wheel that spins inside your minds! Woe to you in the clutch of the scorching that dwells inside you, because it will consume your flesh visibly and rip your souls invisibly, and will make you ready to join your friends! Woe to you prisoners, because you are fettered in caves!
6.6: “You mock, in insane laughter you smirk! You are unaware of your damnation, and you fail to consider your state, and [you] have failed to understand that you live in darkness and [death]! Instead, you are intoxicated with fire and [filled] with bitterness. Your mind is insane because of the [scorching that is inside] you, and the venom and the attacks of your enemies are sweet to you! And the gloom rose for you like the light, because you capitulated your freedom for slavery! You blackened your hearts and relinquished your thoughts to foolishness, and you filled your thoughts with the fiery smoke inside you! And your light [was obscured] in the cloud [of . . .], and the clothes that cover you, you [. . .]. And [you] were captured by a vacuous [hope]. And whom did [you] believe? Do you [not understand that] all of [you] live among those that [. . .] you as though [you . . .].

7.1: [ 144 ] You immersed yourselves in the water of gloom! You acted according to your own urges! Woe to you who live in error, who neglect the light of the sun who judges the world and gazes down at the world, that will encircle all things in order to enslave enemies. Nor do you perceive the moon, who by night and day gazes down, beholding the corpses from your slaughtering! Woe to you who love to be close to women and (who love) unclean intercourse with them! Woe to you caught in the clutch of your bodily powers, because they will torment you! Woe to you caught in the clutch of the forces of evil demons! Woe to you who lure your limbs with fire!
7.2: “Who will send a shower of cool dew on you to quench the cloud of fire engulfing you together with your scorching? Who will make the sun to shine on you to dispel the gloom inside you and to conceal the gloom and impure water? The sun and moon, with the air and the wind, and the earth and the water, will grant you a fragrant scent, because if the sun does not shine on these bodies, they will wilt and perish, exactly like weeds and grass. If the sun shines on them, they take over and strangle the grapevine. If, however, the grapevine takes over and shades all the weeds and other bushes growing next to them, and [spreads] and increases, it will receive the land by itself where it grows and dominate every place where it has overshadowed it. And when it matures, it will control the entire land and will produce bountifully for its master, and will please him yet more, because he will have avoided the great trouble of uprooting these plants. However, the grapevine by itself got rid of them, even choking them, and they died and became as (dead) as the soil.”
7.3: Jesus then continued and said: “Woe to you, because you did not accept the teaching, and those who [. . .] will work at preaching [. . .]. And [you] are running into [. . .] will drive [them] downward [. . .] by day you kill them

58.3: TRUTH, ALĒTHŌS: Here at 41,7 p-aiōn n - me alēthōs , literally “the aeon, the truth truly” (idiomatically, “the aeon, truly the truth”), anticipates the repeated double alēthōs alēthōs in the text’s concluding hymn, which likely echoes and interprets the canonical gospels’ “amen, amen,” from the phrase “amen, amen, I say unto you.” In Codex III the adverb alēthōs occurs alone at 41,7 and 67,13. The phrase alēthes alēthōs (the neuter adjective  alēthes + the adverb alēthōs ), literally “true truly,” or in idiomatic English, “truly true,” occurs at 62,4 and on page 66 in lines 15, 17, 20. The slightly different phrase alēthōs alēthōs , “truly, truly,” “verily, verily,” occurs on page 66 lines 9 and 12, and at 68,1. Codex IV renders both phrases with the Coptic mntme name , literally “truth truly.” The previous standard English rendering of the Greek alēthes alēthōs / alēthōs alēthōs and the Coptic mntme name as “really truly” not only fails to reproduce the grammatical repetition in the Greek and Coptic, but overlooks their function as ritual words of power. I render all these instances in uppercase in order to reflect their status as ritual words of power. This status is clear from the passages where they are associated with other letters and words of power retained in Greek, especially the text’s strings of Greek vowels, which have been compared to glossolalia.

28.2: This passage is cognate to the Synoptic “Little Apocalypse” in Mark 13, Matthew 24, and Luke 21.

28.6: Cf. Luke 17:21; Gospel of Thomas logion 3.

28.16: For the thematic constellation of water, baptism, and wind, cf. John 3:5-7.
28.17: “Extreme edge of heaven and earth,” not “the final end.” We have here a spatial indicator, not a temporal one.
28.18: An echo of Deuteronomy 30:12 via Gospel of Thomas logion 3.
28.19: An echo of Exodus 20:14: “And all the people saw the voices.”
28.20: Cf. Psalm 139:14, “fearfully and wonderfully,” that is, causing or inspiring fear and wonder.
28.21: I have rearranged these four lines, which seem out of order in the codex, where their sequence reads as follows:
28.22: Matthew asked: “Why do we not rest at once?”
28.23: The Lord said: “By leaving behind these burdens.”
28.24: Matthew asked: “How does the small harmonize with the great?”

28.27: The passage echoes Luke 20:4: “Was the baptism of John from Heaven [i.e., God] or from men?” The echo is confirmed by Judas’ question that soon follows on page 144: “When we pray, how should we pray?” This in turn echoes Luke 11:1-2: “He was praying in a certain place, and when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him, ‘Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples.’ / And he said to them, ‘When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be thy name. . . .’” (RSV) Notice the shared lexeme “place” where Jesus prays in Luke 11:1 and Dialogue of the Savior 144, “The Lord said: ‘Pray in the place. . . .’” The Parable of the mustard seed occurs in Luke 13:18-19, rather distant from Luke 11:1-2. I suspect that “Mary asked: ‘[Of what] kind is the mustard seed?” may be a corruption of an original “Mary asked: ‘[Of what] kind is baptism?”
28.28: “Matthew says,” not “Matthew said.” The implication is that The Dialogue of Savior here is quoting from some other text that contains this interpretation of Matthew.
28.30: Coptic kō , not in the sense of “forgive,” but in the sense of “loosen,” i.e., “dissolve (works),” a synonym of the earlier “destroy (works).”

20.3: Following the division of text by Kasser and Funk.
20.7: The text is obscure. Cf. Funk, “I am in a secret [way] the brother who scorned (?).”
20.8: “Hail,” in Hebrew this would be shalom .
20.9: “He is no stranger to us.” I.e., he is a family member.
20.10: Coptic pson [ha] pekeiōt . The preposition ha (Crum 632a-633b) has several potential meanings, including “from” and “by reason of.” Here ha likely renders Greek ek , “from,” “out of,” “by,” including descent from a parent or ancestor, e.g., ek patros , “from a father.” Although “brother of a father” can idiomatically mean “cousin,” most likely the text here should be read straightforwardly. “He is the brother from your father” could conceivably imply the existence of other siblings from a different father.
20.11: This can be glossed as follows: “Your (physical) father is not my (spiritual) father, but my (spiritual) father became a (spiritual) father to you.”
20.14: The vocabulary sounds Enochic; cf. 1 En 58:3,6, which expands 1 En 5:6-9.
20.18: This is usually emended to “I judge <not>.” I find this emendation plausible but ultimately unnecessary.
20.19: I follow Hedrick and do not emend the text, although my interpretation of the text differs from Hedrick’s. We have here an echo of the idiom “the Lord . . . from the Lord” in Gen 19:24’s account of the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. Cf. Rev 11:8’s allegorical designation of Jerusalem as “Sodom.”
20.21: An echo of Isa 6:10 and possibly 44:18 as well.
20.22: The text needs no emendation. As Quispel explains by comparing Gos. Thom . 71 to Jer 7:14 (both about the destruction of the temple), prophets can speak with the divine “I” without introducing it with “Thus says the Lord.” See the chapter “The Gospel of Thomas and the Trial of Jesus” in Gilles Quispel, Gnostica, Judaica, Catholica: Collected Essays of Gilles Quispel Edited by Johannes van Oort (Leiden/Boston: Brill, 2008), 227-235; here 234-235.
20.23: The reconstruction of the lacuna is uncertain.
20.25: Or “Let not your grace be abandoned in me.”
20.26: “Life of life,” probably a Semitic superlative idiom.
